messages:
maya: hitting a weird one in the sampleapp streaming flow — when our proxy returns 429 + Retry-After during a reconnect the client sometimes never resumes the SSE stream. observed on node & python sampleapps. anyone seen this?

josh: can you paste minimal repro steps / logs? also which SDK version?

maya: repro steps: 1) start sampleapp with streaming chat 2) throttle upstream so requests get a 429 with Retry-After: 2 3) client reconnects, we return the last-event-id header but then chunks arrive out of order a bit and parser stalls. logs: 
```
[INFO] reconnecting, lastEventId=evt_123
[WARN] got 429, retry-after=2
[INFO] new connection established
DEBUG chunk: "data: {\"id\":\"evt_124\", \\"delta\\":\"Hel"
DEBUG chunk: "lo\n\n"
ERROR parse: unexpected EOF while waiting for event terminator
```

clara: hm. couple thoughts: 1) do both SDKs include the last-event-id header on the retry? node SDK historically reattaches it, python had a bug where the header was dropped on auth refresh. 2) partial chunk handling: if the connection is closed mid-event we must buffer until we see the full "\n\n" delimiter or carry partial across reconnect.

sam: +1 on buffering. also, rate-limited reconnects can reorder chunks if the proxy does a buffered flush; we ended up seeing a chunk from a previous connection arrive after the retry. adding an incremental sequence/id in the payload helped us detect reorder.

maya: interesting — i can repro with local nginx proxy doing `return 429` with `Retry-After`. node sampleapp version 0.9.1, python SDK 0.6.2. i'll try toggling auth refresh off to see if that changes behavior.

josh: if it's auth refresh related we should test both polyglot SDKs. can you paste the minimal fetch code used by the client?

maya: here's the client reconnect snippet we use in sampleapp: 
```
fetch(url, { headers: { 'Last-Event-Id': lastId, 'Authorization': `Bearer ${token}` }})
```

on reconnect we call the same function again after backoff.

clara: that looks fine. python SDK used to re-create the request object on token refresh and accidentally drop Last-Event-Id. i'll open a quick PR to keep headers consistent across refresh.

sam: for the parser side i can sketch a small change: treat `data:` lines as append-to-buffer until we see the event terminator, and when reconnecting, keep the trailing partial buffer and preprend it to the next connection stream. Also add a short-lived sequence check: if event.id <= lastSeen then drop duplicate, if > lastSeen+1 log reorder. this should make the client robust to interleaved flushes.

maya: happy to run integration test — i'll set up a flaky-proxy job in CI that injects 429 mid-stream and validates we still end up with the same assembled events.

josh: sounds like an action plan: 1) clara will PR header-preserve fix for python SDK 2) sam will PR parser buffering + sequence handling 3) maya will add CI flaky-proxy test and a tiny repro harness we can run locally. can we get these done this week? :crossed_fingers: 

clara: i'll target a tiny change and a unit test today. should be trivial. :thumbsup: 

sam: i'll prototype the buffering behaviour and share a patch tomorrow.

maya: i'll open an issue and link the repro steps + local nginx conf. assigning to me for the repro and CI job.

ci-bot: created issue #1428 (sse: sampleapp stall on 429 reconnect), attached logs and nginx conf.

josh: perfect. once PRs land let's run a canary on the staging sampleapp and then roll to prod. thanks everyone!
